title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
description: Count the connected groups in an undirected graph with vertices numbered from zero through n minus one. Isolated vertices count as components. Edges connect distinct vertices and are not repeated.

examples.raw:
Input: n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[3,4]]
Output: 2
Explanation: Two groups: {0,1,2} and {3,4}.

examples.explain: All vertices connect, so there is one group.
examples.raw:
Input: n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,4]]
Output: 1
Explanation: All vertices connect, so there is one group.

hints: Union the endpoints of every edge, then count distinct roots.
A depth-first walk from each unvisited vertex also counts groups once.
Track visited vertices so an isolated vertex still forms its own group.
solution: Union-find over the edges, then count distinct set leaders; isolated vertices stay singletons. O(n + edges α(n)) time.
